transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

You likely need a new heating element, as this is the most common cause of a tumble dryer running but not producing heat. However, it could also be a faulty thermal fuse or thermostat if those components have failed open. From what you have described, the most likely cause is clean the lint/fluff filter (and condenser filter) and clear the airflow. A blocked lint filter stops the airflow, and many dryers then cut the heat to stop overheating. Clean the fluff filter in the door opening (heat-pump models often have a second one at the bottom too). Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?

Yeah the lint filter was fairly full, I've cleaned it now. Still cold after 20 min though. Also the long vent hose out the window had a sag full of fluff, I've cleared that too. Safe to say that hose was properly clogged before it stopped heating.
From what you have described, the most likely cause is the heater, its thermal cut-out or thermostat. Run a normal heat programme again for 10–15 minutes. Is it heating now, or still cold?
Already did that, ran it 20 min after cleaning and it's still cold. So which part is it, the element or the thermostat? I haven't got a multimeter to test them.

It could be either the heating element or one of the thermostats, as both are common failure points for this symptom. Without a multimeter to test them electrically, you cannot determine which specific component has failed. Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
I can't see a condenser unit or second filter on mine, it's a vented one with a hose out the window. So can you just tell me which part to order? Model on the front says DV7110.

You cannot simply order a replacement part without first identifying the specific failed component, as cold air can be caused by a faulty heating element, thermostat, thermal fuse, or control board. Since you do not have a multimeter to test these parts for continuity, you would need to consult a qualified technician to diagnose which one has actually failed before purchasing anything. From what you have described, the most likely cause is heater element. Some programmes (cool air, refresh, delicates or a low-heat option) dry with little or no heat. Was a cool-air or low-heat programme set (and have you changed it), or was it a normal heat programme?
[Safety panel] Clean the lint filter after every load — a build-up of fluff is a fire risk and restricts airflow. Don't run the dryer overnight or while you're out.
